summary: event-bus-lite-testmetest executes an encrypted ~427KB payload on npm install via binding.gyp command-expansion
details: The package ships a binding.gyp with no native source files; its `sources` entry uses GYP command-expansion (`<!(node index.js...)`) to invoke the shipped index.js at `node-gyp rebuild` time, which npm triggers automatically on install whenever a binding.gyp is present. index.js is a stub that performs two layers of eval: two top-level IIFEs eval the result of a Caesar-cipher transform over large char-code arrays; the decoded JavaScript imports node:crypto, fs, path and zlib, builds an AES-128-GCM decipher with hardcoded key/iv/tag, decrypts a ~427KB ciphertext (with additional encrypted bytes in an adjacent lib_native.dat of ~320KB), and passes the plaintext to eval. The package.json self-identifies as a stub (`"stub": true`, description "placeholder for staged publishing") yet declares a runtime dependency on `bun` (^1.2.18), pulling an alternate language runtime into node_modules alongside the encrypted blob. There is no legitimate native addon being built — the binding.gyp's only purpose is to serve as an install-time execution vector for the obfuscated payload.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
